summary: Latency spike on internal Cost Model API endpoint causing slow Console cost breakdown loads
description:
Issue summary:
- Customer reports Console cost breakdown pages intermittently taking 20–60s to load or timing out.
- Root symptom appears to be elevated p95 latency on internal Cost Model API (estimate/breakdown endpoints), which Console backend calls on-demand.

Customer impact:
- Northbridge Security Labs (enterprise) cannot reliably load Console cost breakdown for the last 24h; internal finance review blocked.
- Console UI shows partial data or "Something went wrong" after ~30s.

Scope / suspected:
- Internal Cost Model API p95 latency spike and occasional 504s between Console backend and cost-model-service.
- Possible regression due to higher request volume and cache-miss heavy query patterns (high-cardinality breakdown dimensions).

Notes:
- This is not a customer calling the Cost Model API directly; it is Console calling internal endpoints on the hot path.
- Console is behind a feature flag for cost-model-backed breakdown; fallback is legacy aggregation if enabled.

Requested outcome:
- Immediate mitigation to restore Console responsiveness.
- Follow-up work: add server-side caching/memoization and enforce tighter request bounding for Console hot paths.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) In prod Console, navigate to Usage → Cost breakdown.
2) Select: Time range = Last 24 hours; Group by = model + route + region (or other multi-dimension view).
3) Observe: UI spinner persists >20s; often times out.

Internal reproduction:
- Hit Console backend endpoint that requests cost-model breakdown for the same range; observe cost-model-service p95 > 8s and occasional gateway timeouts.
expected_result: Console cost breakdown loads in <5s for Last 24 hours views; Cost Model API p95 within SLO.
actual_result: Cost Model API p95 spikes to 8–15s (with tail up to ~30s) leading to Console timeouts/partial results; sporadic 504s.
investigation_notes:
Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-02-18 16:40: Support intake from CSM: Northbridge reports Console cost pages timing out.
- 2026-02-18 17:05: Console team confirms elevated latency calling cost-model-service; opens SUP-31905.
- 2026-02-18 17:20: SRE reviews Grafana dashboard (cost-model API). p95 latency jump coincides with increased request volume after enabling breakdown feature flag for additional orgs.
- 2026-02-18 17:40: Noted many requests with high-cardinality breakdown configs (multiple group_by dimensions) and large time windows returning large intermediate aggregates.
- 2026-02-18 18:05: Checked telemetry/analytics dependency health: ingestion lag within normal bounds; not the primary driver.
- 2026-02-18 18:15: Cost-model-service CPU saturation observed; GC pressure increased; request concurrency spikes.
- 2026-02-18 18:30: Identified Console backend retry behavior amplifying load during slow responses.

Hypotheses evaluated:
- Telemetry lag / backfill causing slow queries: ruled out (lag normal; queries still slow with fresh data).
- Schema negotiation issues causing retries: not primary (version distribution stable; errors not concentrated).
- Cardinality explosion from unbounded breakdown dimensions: likely contributor.
- Missing caching layer for identical repeated queries (Console refresh/polling): confirmed (cache hit rate near zero).

Slack coordination:
- Referenced #incidents thread about cost drift alert/telemetry lag earlier in the week; not directly related but informed mitigation approach.

Customer comms:
- Acknowledged incident, shared mitigation plan: temporarily reduce breakdown complexity and/or fall back to legacy aggregation while performance improvements roll out.
resolution:
Mitigation applied (2026-02-18 19:05 UTC):
- Console: temporarily reduced feature-flag exposure for cost-model-backed breakdown for affected org(s) and enabled legacy fallback for high-latency scenarios.
- Cost-model-service: applied a temporary config to enforce stricter request bounds for breakdown requests coming from Console (max group_by dimensions and max time buckets) per API guidelines.
- Infra: increased service replicas and tightened timeouts to reduce queued tail latency; added circuit-breaker behavior in Console backend to avoid retry amplification.

Result:
- Cost-model-service p95 returned to ~2.1s; 504s stopped.
- Console load times improved to <6s for Northbridge on standard views; advanced high-cardinality view now shows a "refine filters" message rather than timing out.

Customer confirmation:
- 2026-02-19: Northbridge confirmed Console is usable again for finance review; requested ETA for permanent fix/caching improvements.
next_steps:
1) Implement server-side caching/memoization for common Console queries (time-window + org + breakdown config) with bounded TTL and cache-size guards.
2) Add explicit Console guidance and guardrails: default group_by set, maximum dimensions, and proactive UI validation.
3) Update Console backend client usage: backoff + jitter; reduce automatic retries on timeouts; introduce request coalescing.
4) Add alert for cache hit rate and high-cardinality request share; ensure dashboards include request-shape distribution.
5) Post-incident follow-up: document the temporary bounds change and ensure it is captured in cost-model API guidelines as a Console-specific profile.

Owners:
- SRE: Rafael Mendes (monitoring + rollout safety)
- Cost Model API: Ethan Park (caching + bounds)
- Console: Jada Williams / Felix Schneider (client behavior + UI guardrails)
comments: 2026-02-18 16:47 (Chloe Martin): Getting reports from Northbridge that cost breakdown pages are timing out. We see a spike in calls to cost-model-service when loading Usage/Cost pages. Can SRE help triage p95? Customer impact: finance review today.

2026-02-18 17:12 (Rafael Mendes): On it. Looking at cost-model API dashboard now. p95 is ~12s over last hour; error rate low but timeouts at gateway are rising. Will dig into request patterns and saturation.

2026-02-18 17:33 (Felix Schneider): Console backend logs show long tail from /internal/cost-model/v1/breakdown. We also retry on timeout (2x). Might be amplifying traffic. We can hotfix to reduce retries if needed.

2026-02-18 18:02 (Ethan Park): Seeing many breakdown requests with 3–4 group_by dimensions + fine-grained buckets. This is worst-case for aggregation. We don’t have caching yet; identical queries repeat on refresh and navigation.

2026-02-18 18:41 (Rafael Mendes): Proposed mitigation: (1) shrink feature-flag exposure for cost-model breakdown; (2) enforce stricter bounds for Console caller; (3) scale replicas. Chloe/Felix please confirm legacy fallback still acceptable for customer until caching ships.
2026-02-18 18:55 (Chloe Martin): Confirmed. We can route Northbridge to legacy breakdown (with a banner) as an interim. Proceed with bounds + scaling now.
2026-02-18 19:18 (Rafael Mendes): Mitigation deployed. p95 trending down to ~2–3s; no new 504s observed. Monitoring for 30 minutes before declaring stable.
2026-02-19 09:10 (Chloe Martin): Northbridge confirmed pages load again. They asked if we can avoid removing advanced group_by options long-term; told them we’re adding caching + performance work.
2026-02-20 14:05 (Rafael Mendes): Closing as mitigated and stable. Follow-ups tracked with platform team; recommend adding cache hit-rate panel and request-shape guardrail metrics to dashboards.
